title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on last week's reliability incident: timeout/5xx spike during heavy batch run. Reviewed root cause (autoscaler threshold + retry storm), temporary mitigations applied, longer-term fixes proposed (adjust autoscaler, rate-limit backoff, dedicated pool for high-throughput routes). Agreed next steps: run benchmarks, config changes, security doc request.
action_items: Priya Shah (Redwood SE): run 100k-token concurrency benchmark with new autoscale thresholds and share raw logs by 2026-03-10
Ben Tran (Lakeview SRE): provide client side retry config and traffic shape sample by 2026-03-09
Alex Morgan (AE): send updated pricing for dedicated pool + burst buffer and link to SOC2 docs by 2026-03-08
next_steps: Run benchmark with adjusted autoscale thresholds (Priya)
Customer to test adjusted client backoff helpers and report if 429/5xx reduce (Ben)
Schedule follow-up to review benchmark results (Alex to propose time)
Customer to request security package if they decide to progress to Dedicated
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO - Lakeview), Asha Patel (Lead ML Engineer), Ben Tran (SRE)

Summary (auto): Follow-up on last week's incident where a burst of requests during nightly batch caused timeouts and a 5xx spike. Discussed root cause, short-term mitigations, and longer-term actions.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Short agenda — incident recap, what we changed, proposed fixes, and next steps. Carlos, do you want to kick off with how you saw the outage from your side?

[00:18] Carlos Mendes: Yeah thanks Alex. So at ~01:30 UTC on Tuesday we had our end-of-day ingestion that starts hitting the inference route. We saw a bunch of 504s and some 5xxs back to back. Basically the client retried a lot, and that made it worse. Our monitoring shows a sharp increase in concurrent requests from the batch job.

[00:34] Asha Patel: And just to add — the batch is highly parallel, like dozens of workers, each doing big prompts. It was the worst-case sequence length, so KV cash was pretty huge — I mean "KV cache", sorry — and the latency ballooned.

[00:50] Priya Shah: Totally, that aligns with what we saw in the Redwood logs. The serving nodes started hitting near their max token memory and our autoscaler was slow to spin up additional instances because the scale policy is CPU based. Also note there was an interaction with the retry storm — client retries were exponential but with a small jitter so many retried at similar intervals.

[01:12] Ben Tran: Right, and we had a mix of 429s and 5xxs. The 429s came from rate limits we have on the hosted route, and the 5xxs were primarily OOM-ish errors or timeouts server-side.

[01:30] Alex Morgan: Ok, good. Quick question — Priya, in the logs is it obvious whether the 5xxs were originating from serving runtime or from the gateway/proxy layer?

[01:44] Priya Shah: Mostly from the runtime — stack traces show kernel-level OOM and some timeouts in the KV cache retrieval path. There's a smaller tail from nginx timeouts at the proxy when the node was unhealthy. We captured request IDs; I can share the raw logs.

[02:05] Carlos Mendes: We noticed the autoscale policy is fairly conservative to avoid cost runaways. But that meant it stayed at baseline until the queue got deep. By the time new instances came up, the backlog had triggered retries.

[02:22] Alex Morgan: Right, so two levers — make autoscaler more responsive for that route, and reduce retry impact via client-side backoff and server-side throttling. Priya, what are candidate changes on the Redwood side?

[02:33] Priya Shah: Short term we recommended bumping the min replicas for that route and adding a burst buffer — Redwood Dedicated can provide a reserved burst pool, but on hosted we can config warm gorups — um warm groups, sorry — warm instances and reduce cold start time. Also change scale from pure CPU to a custom metric e.g., queue depth or token memory.

[02:58] Asha Patel: If we bump min replicas that will increase cost; we need a sense of the delta. Alex, can you share pricing for a small dedicated pool vs raising min replicas on hosted?

[03:10] Alex Morgan: Yep I'll send a comparison after the call — quick note though, Dedicated gives isolated capacity and predictable latency which avoids noisy neighbours; but there's a commit cost. I'll include numbers.

[03:22] Ben Tran: On the client side we've already pushed a small change: increase base backoff and add jitter. We'll run another nightly job with that change. We'll also add a 429-specific exponential backoff rather than blanket immediate retry.

[03:35] Carlos Mendes: For visibility we need more granular tracing — the sample IDs showed retries obscuring the initial slow requests. Can Redwood add per-request token counts and memory footprint in the logs?

[03:48] Priya Shah: We can add token_count and kv_cache_size to the request metadata in logs for the POC. It'll increase log volume but should help root cause. I'll enable that for the route for the next 48 hours.

[04:03] Alex Morgan: Great. Now let's walk through the mitigations timeline — what was applied already and what we propose. Priya?

[04:12] Priya Shah: Immediately after the incident we added a temporary rate-limit rule to reject large concurrent batch workers by returning a 429 sooner, and we bumped the route's min instances from 2 to 4 for the night window. That reduced the 5xx tail. For longer term, proposals are: 1) change autoscaler metric to queue depth/token memory, 2) enable KV cache eviction policy tuned for your sequence lengths, 3) consider a small Dedicated pool or reserved burst capacity, 4) client-side retry helpers and 5) better tracing/logging.

[04:52] Asha Patel: That eviction policy — does Redwood have a knob for prioritizing short-running requests in the KV cache? We have a mix of large batch and real-time calls from customers. We don't want the batch to evict everything for the short requests.

[05:06] Priya Shah: Yes, we have LRU with per-route weights; we can tune weights so real-time user-facing routes get higher priority. Also batching policy can be separated by route so batch jobs can be offloaded to a different pool.

[05:20] Ben Tran: Offloading batch sounds attractive. Would that require a Dedicated pool or can hosted do route isolation?

[05:28] Alex Morgan: You can do route isolation on hosted by setting separate model variants and allocation policies — but on hosted there's still multi-tenant hardware. For strict isolation Dedicated is the recommended path.

[05:41] Carlos Mendes: Also, given compliance we might need to move to VPC for some datasets later. That would push us toward Private deployment. For now it's not required but good to know the path.

[05:52] Alex Morgan: Understood. We'll include Private/VPC notes in the security pack.

[06:00] Asha Patel: One question about retries — our current client lib retries 3 times with fixed backoff. Is there a Redwood-recommended pattern?

[06:09] Priya Shah: We recommend jittered exponential backoff with a max retries around 4 for 5xx and indefinite for idempotent requests depending on your use case. Also implement client-side rate limiting to shape traffic — we can share a small backoff helper snippet.

[06:26] Alex Morgan: I'll attach that helper in the follow-up. Ben, you said you'll test an updated backoff tonight?

[06:31] Ben Tran: Yes, we'll run it in canary for the next overnight window and report results tomorrow morning.

[06:39] [09:00] Priya Shah: Sorry small correction — I meant we'll enable the token_count and kv_cache_size fields now and collect for next two runs. Also I'll create a short runbook describing which metrics to watch: queue depth, token memory, instance spin-up time, 429 rate.

[06:58] Carlos Mendes: Cool. Another thing — during the incident the dashboard didn't show per-route spin-up latency. Can that be surfaced in Console?

[07:06] Alex Morgan: We do have per-route metrics in Redwood Console but not the exact spin-up latency as a separate metric by default. We can add a synthetic metric for instance warm-up time and expose it on your dashboard for the POC. Priya will set that up.

[07:18] Priya Shah: Yup I'll add it and send a dashboard link.

[07:24] Asha Patel: About the 5xx classification — can Redwood provide a breakdown of 5xx types so we can see OOM vs timeout vs internal error? That would help prioritize fixes.

[07:34] Priya Shah: Yes we already parsed stack traces; I'll add a breakdown to the logs view and the CSV export.

[07:43] Alex Morgan: Great. Let's talk about the benchmark Priya mentioned — what will you run and what do you expect to measure?

[07:50] Priya Shah: We'll run a synthetic workload that mirrors your nightly batch: same concurrency, same sequence length distribution, and same token counts. We'll run it across three configs: baseline (current autoscale), aggressive autoscale (lower scale threshold, higher max replicas), and dedicated-like with reserved burst. The output will be latency P95/P99, 5xx counts, and cost estimate.

[08:12] Carlos Mendes: And will you include client retry behavior in the benchmark? We want to see its effect on the system under load.

[08:19] Priya Shah: Yes we'll run versions with and without client retries to show the difference. We'll also capture trace IDs so you can correlate.

[08:28] Ben Tran: For the record, our night job windows are 01:00-02:30 UTC. If you can run benchmarks to simulate that slope it would be helpful.

[08:36] Priya Shah: Got it. We'll align to that window. Expect results by 2026-03-10.

[08:43] Alex Morgan: Ok, next up — security/compliance asks you had earlier, Carlos?

[08:49] Carlos Mendes: Yes, we need the SOC2 artifacts and an architecture note for VPC egress. Also want to confirm data retention for logs and whether token-level traces include PII.

[09:01] Alex Morgan: We'll send the SOC2 package and a short VPC architecture doc. On logs — default logs do not include customer prompt text, but we can enable token_count and size metrics; we can also redact request bodies in logs. We'll include retention options.

[09:18] Asha Patel: For the POC we need 30-day log retention with the ability to pull CSVs for the incident window.

[09:25] Alex Morgan: Noted — we'll set retention to 30 days for the route for the POC.

[09:30] Priya Shah: One more thing — on the runtime side, we've got an experimental quantization profile that lowers memory by ~20% for your model family. That could reduce the KV cache footprint. But we need to validate quality. Would you like us to run a quality regression on a small eval set?

[09:47] Asha Patel: Yes, please. We can't accept regression beyond 1% at P95. If you can run the eval and share diffs that'd be ideal.

[09:58] Priya Shah: We'll run the eval and include quality metrics, then you can decide whether to adopt the quantized variant in POC.

[10:06] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. Back to next steps — can we recap owners and due dates?

[10:11] Alex Morgan: Sure. Priya to run the benchmark and enable extra logging by 2026-03-10. Ben to test client backoff and provide traffic shape by 2026-03-09. Alex to send pricing, SOC2, and security pack by 2026-03-08. Anything else?

[10:29] Ben Tran: I'll also provide the exact worker concurrency numbers and a sample of the job config.

[10:35] Asha Patel: I'll collect an evaluation set and share with Priya for the quantization quality run.

[10:41] Alex Morgan: Great. Anything else from the team?

[10:44] [Silence / small crosstalk]

[10:48] Carlos Mendes: No, that's it. Appreciate the quick response from Redwood on the mitigations.

[10:54] Alex Morgan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule a results review next week. I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute review after the benchmark completes.

[11:04] Priya Shah: I'll post the dashboard link and raw logs to the shared folder.

[11:09] Alex Morgan: Perfect. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" for "KV cache", occasional speaker labels generic). Logs and full trace IDs shared in follow-up link: https://redwood.link/ff-logs-45231 (note: placeholder).
